newsitem.title: SPAIN: GOLF-LAST VOLVO MASTERS FOR VALDERRAMA.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-LAST VOLVO MASTERS FOR VALDERRAMA.

text.p: The Volvo Masters will not return to the Valderrama course after Sunday's final round although the venue could host a future World Tour event.
The prestigious final event of the European Tour season will be held next year at another course still to be announced, with Quinta do Lago in Portugal the favourite.
"It is the end of a chapter, the best nine years I have ever had," said course owner and Bolivian tin millionaire Jaime Ortiz Patino.
"Without the Volvo Masters we would never have been able to get the Ryder Cup.
"After nine years with the best players in Europe and after the Ryder Cup with the best from Europe and the United States, what can I do after that?

"There is only one thing I can hope for, and for which the club is available if required, and that is a tournament with the best players from Europe, North America and the rest of the World," he added in a reference to the World Tour which is expected to begin within the next few years.
Patino said he envisaged few changes to the course for the Ryder Cup with no alterations planned for the controversial 17th hole.
The hole was criticised last year and this week because of the humps on the landing areas of the fairway and the steep slope down from the green to a lake in front of it.
"The hole was designed by (Ryder Cup captain) Seve Ballesteros," Patino said. "If he wants me to change something I will do it with pleasure.
"I made a few changes last year. If he tells me tomorrow he is no longer pleased with the hole we will make the changes he requires."
Patino said there could be some bottlenecks for fans on a layout not regarded as a prime viewing course.
"This is not a stadium course but no recent Ryder Cup venue has been a stadium course," he said.
He said provision was being made to erect grandstands at various points around the course and everything would be done to provide ready access to all parts of it.
European Tour executive director Ken Schofield praised both the course, which will host next year's Ryder Cup between Europe and the United States, and the tournament.

"The Volvo Masters at Valderrama has elevated our Tour to something that, before the arrival of Volvo, before the arrival of Valderrama, was simply a dream. They've made it a reality and we salute them," he said.
